newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean core inflation seen rising - report.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean core inflation seen rising - report.

text.p: South Korea, which has enjoyed a slowdown in inflation growth since the early 1990s, is beginning to experience an upswing in its core inflation rate, the LG Economic Research Institute said in a report.

The report, released this week by the Seoul-based group, said South Korea's core inflation rate was expected to exceed the consumer price index (CPI) by one percentage point this year after growing steadily since mid-1994.
The core inflation rate, which strips out items typically sensitive to external shocks, ran at 5.3 percent in 1995 compared to a CPI rate of 4.5 percent, LG said.
It expected the core rate to rise even further this year to 6.4 percent.
"Compared to the early 1990s inflation rate of 8-9 percent, recent figures between 4.5-5.0 percent certainly indicate that inflation is indeed taming down," the report said.

"The exceptional stability of prices last year in the midst of a rapid economic growth rate of over nine percent brought on hasty expectations of the arrival of an era of rapid growth and low prices that we observe in more mature economies," it said.
"However, a more close examination of the consumer price index portrays somewhat different behavior of the inflation trend," the report added.
It said the core inflation rate adjusted for irregularities such as oil price increases and poor weather, which were beyond the control of monetary authorities, represented a more stable trend.
